why: Heights can only grow, so the ascending target is final[i] = b + i for some base b. The cost is the sum of (b + i - s[i]), which is smallest when b is as small as allowed, b = max(s[i] - i). Descending works the same way with b = max(s[i] + i). Take the cheaper of the two. This week is Greedy + Math: the greedy choice is the smallest feasible base.
hints: Once you fix the first height of a stepwise array, every other height is fixed too.
Every element needs b + i >= s[i], so b >= s[i] - i. The cost grows with b, so choose the smallest feasible b.
In one pass compute b_up = max(s[i]-i) and b_down = max(s[i]+i), then cost = n*b +/- n(n-1)/2 - sum(s). Answer = min of the two. O(n) time, O(1) space.
pitfalls: You cannot lower any height, so the base is pinned by the most demanding element, not by the first one.
Results can exceed 32-bit (the return type is long). Python is fine, but watch it in other languages.
